ExplainabilityCoverage.description:
The ``ensemble_shap_coverage`` block on the explainability payload
(P6b) — normalised to FRACTIONS in [0, 1] with documented keys, plus the
``source`` flag so the UI can say where the numbers come from.

- ``source="recomputed"`` — computed by the backend from the weights of
  the actually-loaded (post-pruning, renormalised) ensemble via the ONE
  shared function (``landval.modelling.coverage``).  ``explained_members``
  / ``unexplained_members`` list the real kept members in this case.
- ``source="manifest"`` — the notebook-time values from
  ``manifest.json:ensemble_shap_coverage`` (pre-pruning), normalised to
  fractions (values above 1 are treated as percentages).  Members are
  ``None`` in this case: the manifest does not record them, and the
  backend never invents member names.
- ``source=None`` — neither path produced shares (e.g. the manifest block
  is absent and the model registry is not loaded).

unexplained_members.description: Kept members SHAP does not cover (source='recomputed' only).

ExplainabilityResponse.description:
GET /api/v1/model/explainability — combines shap_global,
feature_importance and feature_labels in one payload so the tab can
render the global-importance chart and the plain-English feature
labels in a single round-trip.

P6b additions (all nullable / defaulting, additive — older payloads
without them still validate):
- ``models`` — the ensemble member list (key, display_name, family,
  ensemble_weight, has_shap), ordered by ensemble weight descending.
  Built from the loaded registry when available, else from the
  distinct models in shap_global.csv (weights null).
- ``default_model`` — the SHAP-covered member with the highest
  ensemble weight (the bars card's default selection); the first
  SHAP-covered member in file order when no weights are available;
  null when no member has SHAP rows.
- ``ensemble_shap_coverage`` — see ``ExplainabilityCoverage``.
- ``typical_price_per_acre_ksh`` / ``combined_base_value`` — the
  load-time baseline price (exp of the weighted sum of tree-member
  base values — the SAME baseline every /predict response reports).
  Null when the model registry / explanation service is unavailable
  (never invented).

MetricsResponse.description:

P5b additions (all nullable, additive):
- ``ensemble_model`` — the production run's ensemble row's model
  name (identified by the backend), null when no such row exists.
  The frontend resolves the ensemble row by THIS value only (no
  substring/heuristic fallbacks).
- ``production_run_label`` — the production run's name + created
  date from the response, for the card subtitle.
- ``interval_levels`` — the nominal interval coverage levels present
  in the data: derived from
  ``metrics_json.interval_coverage_weighted_ensemble[*].level`` when
  the artifact carries them; else from the ensemble row's populated
  ``interval_coverage_*`` columns; else null.
- ``interval_method`` — documented backend constant describing the
  interval implementation (the modeling code implements the
  multiplicative split-conformal interval — see
  ``src/landval/modelling/predict.py``); null when unknown.
- ``n_test`` / ``n_dev`` — row counts of the loaded prediction
  parquets (test_predictions / oof_predictions); null when the file
  is not loaded.
- ``model_info`` — per-model ``display_name`` + ``family`` from the
  backend's documented model registry mapping (facts about the
  model implementations, not UI copy).
- ``default_interval_level`` — the app's standard level (the same
  canonical constant the predict options endpoint serves).

TrendBlock.description:
Log-linear fit of price per acre against distance over ALL filtered
rows (so the chart's trend line does not depend on the scatter sample).

Model: ``log(price) = slope * distance_km + intercept``.  ``r2`` is the
coefficient of determination of the fit (1.0 = perfect, 0.0 = no
linear relationship, negative = worse than predicting the mean).

intercept.description: log(price) at distance=0.  Null when < 2 rows.

r2.description: Coefficient of determination.  Null when < 2 rows.

VerdictOption.description:
One verdict + its data-derived definition.

``rule`` carries the REAL thresholds observed in the frame, so the UI
can template "listed at least X% below predicted" without typing a
percentage:

- ``basis`` — "conformal_interval": the verdict reproduces the
  listed-price-vs-interval comparison (below low / within /
  above high) on every row where it could be checked.
- ``match_rate`` — the share of rows where the comparison above
  reproduces the stored verdict (1.0 = exact).
- ``under_ratio_max`` — the maximum listed_over_predicted ratio
  observed among underpriced rows (the empirical cut-off).
- ``over_ratio_min`` — the minimum ratio among overpriced rows.
- ``interval_low_ref`` / ``interval_high_ref`` — the frame column
  names the comparison uses (documented, not magic).
VerdictOption.title: VerdictOption

interval_high_ref.description: Frame column used as the interval upper bound
interval_high_ref.title: Interval High Ref

interval_low_ref.description: Frame column used as the interval lower bound
interval_low_ref.title: Interval Low Ref

match_rate.description: Share of rows where the rule reproduces the stored verdict
match_rate.title: Match Rate

VerdictsBlock.description:
Counts + shares of the stored ``verdict`` column (Underpriced /
Fair / Overpriced).  Shares are computed from the filtered usable
rows and sum (with n_unknown) to n_listings.

n_listings.description: Filtered usable row count (shares are over this)
n_listings.title: N Listings

n_unknown.description: Rows whose verdict is not one of the three known values
n_unknown.title: N Unknown

get.description:
Per-county listing counts from ``listings_scored.parquet`` — for the
scatter-plot tab's county picker + the "N listings" label.

This does NOT return medians (those come from /counties/summary).  It
only reports how many listings each county has in the per-listing
endpoint's backing frame, so the frontend can warn when a county's
coverage is thin.

One row per county (optionally filtered by prop_type), plus the
canonical property-type list, data-driven price bands, and the
min_county_n threshold from the artifact config.

**Filtering:** when ``prop_type`` is set, the per-county aggregates
are recomputed from the filtered ``listings_scored`` frame (the
pre-aggregated ``county_summary.csv`` cannot be filtered).  The two
paths agree on the shared columns; the frame path leaves
``water_body_distance_share`` null (that column is notebook-only).

**Price bands (P3b):** the band edges are quintiles of the medians
of the counties that meet ``min_county_n`` — equal county-frequency
bands, recomputed when the filter changes so the legend always
matches the map.

get.description:
Per-listing scatter-plot data for one county.

Returns ``price_per_acre_ksh``, ``dist_to_nairobi_km`` (recomputed from
lat/lon via B1's haversine), ``size_acres``, and ``verdict`` for each
listing in the county.  Backed by ``listings_scored.parquet`` (Cell 9.6)
— the only export that carries ``listed_price_per_acre_ksh`` +
``size_acres`` together.  The prediction parquets (oof/test) lack
``size_acres`` and only carry ``y_true`` (log scale), not the asking
price per acre.

**Medians / IQR for the ranked list and deep-dive cards come from
/counties/summary (county_summary.csv) — this endpoint does NOT
recompute them.**

Log-scale price histogram + percentiles over the usable listings.

``flag_definition`` (P7b) carries the flagged-listing rule (the
percentile window from the canonical constants) so the frontend can
explain what "flagged as possible errors" means without typing
"1st–99th".

Liveness + readiness probe.

Returns ``status: ok`` when all artifacts are loaded **and** the model
registry successfully loaded the ensemble (so ``/api/v1/predict`` is
usable).  ``degraded`` covers two cases:

1. The ``ArtifactRegistry`` (B0) found a missing top-level file
   (``xgb_model.json``, ``preprocessing.json``, …).
2. The ``ModelRegistry`` (this phase) raised ``ModelLoadError`` —
   typically because ``serving_manifest.json`` or one of the model
   files it lists is missing, or because the feature pipeline's
   ``scoring_params.json`` / ``reference_data.json`` /
   ``feature_manifest.json`` are absent.

In both cases the app still starts so ``/docs`` and the test suite
work without the large model files.

Read-only option lists + limits + availability flags for the Deal
Finder UI.  Everything the filters bar renders comes from here — the
frontend never re-types a list.
Paginated + filtered Deal Finder table with server-side sorting.

Streaming CSV of every row matching the current filters.

- Same filter/sort semantics as /listings/scored (single source of
  truth — the same validation code path runs).
- Header row, UTF-8 with BOM (Excel-friendly); money columns are raw
  KSh numbers so Excel can sum them.
- A row cap ONLY when configured via the ``LISTINGS_EXPORT_MAX_ROWS``
  setting (default: no cap).  When the cap truncates the export, the
  response carries ``X-Export-Truncated: true`` and
  ``X-Export-Total`` headers rather than silently cutting.
- ``Content-Disposition`` filename is built from the active filters.

excluding the listing itself.  Unknown listing -> 404; a listing with
missing coordinates -> an empty list with a ``reason``.

get.description:
Return lightweight artifact metadata + FX + canonical copy blocks.

When artifacts are not loaded (degraded mode) the model_version /
data_date / coverage / ensemble_weights fields are ``null``.  The FX
block comes from settings (env), NOT artifacts — but there is no
default rate in code, so it too is ``null`` until the operator
configures one.  ``flag_definition`` and ``methodology`` are code
constants and are always served.

OOF error broken down by listing-count support bands.

Returns ``error_by_support.csv`` (Cell 9.9) — two groups of bands:
- ``county_listings``: error by the number of listings in the county
  (<10 / 10-19 / 20-49 / 50+)
- ``nearby_within_50km``: error by the number of listings within 50km
  (<5 / 5-9 / 10-19 / 20-49 / 50+)

Global mean-|SHAP| + native & permutation importance + feature labels.

P6b additions: ``models`` (the ensemble member list with display names,
families, weights and a has_shap flag) + ``default_model``; the
``ensemble_shap_coverage`` block is now normalised to fractions with a
``source`` flag — recomputed from the actually-loaded ensemble's weights
when the model registry is loaded (the same shared computation the live
/predict coverage block uses), else the notebook-time manifest values;
``typical_price_per_acre_ksh`` / ``combined_base_value`` carry the
load-time baseline when the explanation service is available.
Phase 3 ranked feature table (Cell 3.8, written by Cell 9.3).

CV + test metrics with bootstrap CIs, ensemble weights, interval coverage.

P5b additions: ``ensemble_model`` (the production run's ensemble row,
identified by the backend — the frontend resolves the row by this
value only, no substring heuristics), ``production_run_label``,
``interval_levels`` (derived from the data — see the schema),
``default_interval_level``, ``interval_method`` (documented backend
constant), ``n_test`` / ``n_dev`` (row counts of the loaded
prediction parquets), and ``model_info`` (per-model display_name +
family from the backend's documented registry mapping).

Per-listing actual vs. predicted values for both splits.

Returns both the development-set out-of-fold predictions and the test-set
predictions in one payload.  Each row carries the identifier columns
(listing_url, listing_no, county, prop_type, etc.) so the frontend can
link a scatter point back to its listing.

post.description:
Predict the price per acre of a Kenyan land parcel.

Returns 503 ``MODEL_NOT_LOADED`` when the ensemble is not loaded
(degraded mode — copy the artefacts into ``ARTIFACTS_DIR`` and restart).
The live explanation and comparables blocks are added when their
respective services are available; they degrade to ``null`` / ``[]``
independently (e.g. when ``listings_scored.parquet`` is missing the
prediction still returns, just without comparables).
